## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ekagāmantara-sikkhāpada* constitutes the third *saṅghādisesa* (suspension) training rule for nuns in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. According to the rule, a bhikkhunī who journeys by herself into an uninhabited or separate village area (*ekagāmantara*), or who stays the night away alone, incurs a serious offense entailing formal meetings of the Saṅgha [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations of the text include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this offense is widely attested across early Buddhist Vinaya traditions, though recensions group or divide its provisions in varied ways [SuttaCentral]. While the Pali Prātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-pm-ss3*) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Saṅghādisesa 3) preserve it as *Ekagāmantara*, corresponding rules appear in the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Ss 7*), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Ss6*), and Sarvāstivāda traditions (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Ss6*; Sanskrit fragments *san-sarv-bi-pm-tf3215-ss6* and *tf44-ss6*) [SuttaCentral]. In the Mūlasarvāstivāda and Mahāsāṅghika/Lokottaravāda traditions, aspects of these prohibitions are divided into related rules regarding solitary travel (*Ekagāmantara*, *Ekagamana*), spending the night alone (*Ekarattivippavāsa*), and crossing a river alone (*Ekanaditara*) in their Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions [SuttaCentral].

Textual alignments generated by DharmaNexus reflect extensive formulaic reuse within the Pali canonical Vinaya, recording over 1,200 shared passages across 165 texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest matches involve shared legal definitions and procedural formulas recurring in other Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules, notably Pācittiya 15, 18, 20, and 60, as well as the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (e.g., Pācittiya 46) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also confirms significant cross-linguistic alignment with northern Vinaya texts, showing substantial textual correspondence with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) and Sanskrit Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* fragments [DharmaNexus].
